newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end up on late blue chips buying.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end up on late blue chips buying.

text.p: The Philippine equities market snapped out of its six day losing streak by closing up on Wednesday, mostly on late-session buying on selected blue chips, brokers said.
Penny stocks still persisted in raking gains but there was gradual accumulation on main liners such as San Miguel Corp, Ayala Land B and PLDT.
Index closed at 3,316.34, up 9.91 points, or 0.30 percent.

"Most plays were centered on secondliner issues during the session but there was accumulation in some blue chips towards the end of the session," said Ramon Garcia, President, Diversified Securities Inc.
Ayala Land B rose by 50 centavo to 30.50 pesos, San Miguel Corp A by one peso to 54.50 pesos and PLDT by ten pesos to 1,560 pesos.

Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital Equities, said trading volume was heavy at 38.937 billion shares valued at 4.898 billion pesos on account of continued focus on speculative and secondliner counters.

"We may see follow-through buying tommorrow on the issues which were bought up late in the session. Over the past two weeks, we have been going sideways down with emphasis on penny stocks, so it may be time for investors to go back to value issues," said Benedict de Borja, analyst at Dharmala Securities Phils Inc.
